chunks.text: Namaste, hello everyone. Welcome to my NPTEL course on Interior Design.
Today we are going to talk about case studies and examples in lecture number 4 and we will
see some very interesting projects. So, for contents I have today some residential building
projects, luxury interiors, low cost interiors, an outdoor cafe, some international commercial
projects, commercial projects in India and some references.
Let us see some residential building projects first. So, this is 4 Leaves Villa and the architects
are KIS, it is a Japan based project and to just give the idea of the area, it is 225
square meters in area and the year of construction is 2018. And it is located in Japan, it is
you know in the middle of a forest and it is a very very interesting sort of a retreat
you know which capitalizes on the natural environment at a mountain retreat which is
150 kilometers away from Tokyo. And what you see over here interestingly is you know that
there are roofs which are designed as curved surfaces like gently twisted leaves and this
gives a very interesting form to the overall you know built form. And there is a combination
of concave and convex roofs that we see over here and again it is like you know overall
very interesting and very sort of full of mystery until and unless we are in the space
it is difficult to understand whether it is compact or expensive, but the overall form
itself is quite mysterious and interesting. These are some of the images of the project
and I find these wooden joists very very interesting. So, there is a series of wooden joists which
is exposed you know on the ceiling and it gives some kind of a dynamism to this entire
space and there is this very interesting character the living space acquires because of this
dynamism. This is the site plan and we can see again the dynamism in terms of you know
the way the blocks are placed. And I always talk about interior architecture which begins
you know from the site planning. So, we will be talking about projects in terms of interior
architecture and we will try to see some structural details all the way to some maybe decorative
panels, but it is like an entire package like we always say why interior architecture and
not as much interior design or interior decor. So, the site is treated very interestingly over
here and this is a scale model which itself is like a you know delight to watch.
There is another project which is the container house it is in Brazil, it is 60 square meters
and it is from the year 2019. So, this is quite compact and here what has happened is that the
architect has tried to transform the shipping containers into a very very modern and functional
house. And the time frame for elaboration and execution of this model of construction is quite
small, quite clean, fast, dry and within the 100 percent reuse of materials. So, there are like
you know two 40 feet containers which are attached alongside and there are spaces which are generated.
So, living space, kitchen space, laundry, a comfortable bathroom etcetera. So, it is a
example and demonstration of reuse and we see a lot of use of shades of white again it makes the
space look quite expensive and big. So, that is again a strategy by design.
And the house has very interesting external area which is very very pleasing you know and it has
this sort of a bench which is sculpted in Brazilian granite and on top of it there are 204
identical stone plates which sort of frame this spiraling impact on that. Then there is this YAO
residence and this is in Thailand, this is 1300 square meters quite big compared to the previous
projects and this is 2019. And again the site placement, the overall landscape and the way the
built form is shaped in terms of the mass and void and the punctures and the fascia of the entire
you know building blocks that is very very interesting. And there is a profound emphasis
you know on the courtyard and we are talking about this interior architecture vocabulary.
So, again focusing on the courtyard, the play of light, the and shadow, the entry of the sunlight
and you know when the rain falls, the falling of rain and its sounds etcetera.
All of those sensory experiences have been sort of captured over here and this sort of
forms the center of the building. Some more images like a very huge floor plate with these nice views
outside you know the pebbles, the entire setting, the stepped seating, all of those interesting
dimensions through which this entire space is designed. And continuing with the interior
architecture vocabulary and the expression you know that we get in a space through different
elements that we put together, it becomes very very important that the entire structure is also
thought about. So, again in terms of like thinking about an interior space architecturally, thinking
in terms of structure, thinking in terms of the overall planning from site all the way to the
you know coasters kept on the table. So, that is interior architecture and that is the demonstration
over here in this project. Some more images. Then there is this another project which we are
talking about today. This is Akelko house and it is Mexico, it is also compact 90 meter square 2017.
And here if you see again it is such a compact space, but again utilizing the settings of the
site and very interesting sort of you know utilization of the surrounding space and
closeness to nature and the kind of retreat. So, like it is a holiday home and therefore,
we see this kind of a setting more so meaningful for this kind of a project completely disconnected
from the city in the middle of the nature. And it works as a resting space actually. So,
it is close to impressive cliffs and it is a very interesting space. And another important aspect
is that the construction is based on solid quarry block walls you know and there are mud floors
over here and these block walls that we see here. And there are lots of materials which
are used here and they are preserved in their natural you know state. There is also a use of
wooden glass. So, the material pallet is very interesting and there is an attempt to preserve
the materials in their natural state. Then some of the luxury interiors we can see over here.
This is a project Mission Hills in Canada and it has some very interesting features.
Now, actually what is happening here is that the ceiling heights approximately 9 feet
and they exclude like low headroom areas due to mechanical systems and therefore,
the ceiling dropped areas. So, whenever we talk about you know these mechanical systems and servicing
because of that the height of the ceiling gets impacted of course, and therefore,
we have to design in that manner. And they have used baseboards throughout this home which are
almost like 5 inches and they are complemented by sort of 3 inches casings you know on windows,
doorways and flat arches to give us sort of a design vocabulary and definition.
So, again to consider some of the interior features, interior doors and trim to be painted white was
a decision. Interior walls also to be painted like of white. So, these are sort of shades of white.
Then natural oak veneer stairs. So, in the lecture we where we concentrate on material timber we are
going to understand the veneers the laminates etcetera. So, there is a natural oak veneer stairs
and then there is also the application of natural oak you know pickets and handrails.
So, these are some very very interesting features and design elements that we see over here.
And of course, you know to get a good oak veneer finish is sort of a luxury. So,
in that sense these are some superior interior features that we see in this project.
There is also a dual panel square interior door and rather doors within this project
with executive style complementary hardware. So, even hardware design is an important aspect
when we talk about interior architecture. So, they have been taken care of the interior doors
are dual panel squares and they are also very interesting. There is like a smooth ceiling
you know and it is seen everywhere throughout the first floor all the ceilings that we see
there on the first floor. Second floor, third floor and the finished basement areas they were to be
stipple spray with smooth borders except lavatories and laundry areas which have smooth ceilings.
So, this was a kind of design vocabulary which was you know sort of established by the designers.
There are some convenient closet organizers over here there is an electric fireplace which is
interesting. When we specifically focus on doors and windows with more level of detailing
there are oversized casement windows throughout which give a very interesting character. All
windows you know they have vinyl low e and you know they are argon gas filled. So, these are also
very technical details in the field of interior design. We try to have like low volatile organic
compounds we try to have more finishes which are you know better suited to health and so on. So,
we have that in one of the modules where we talk about green interiors. Then there is an insulated
front entrance door which has a magnificent glass insert detail and it looks quite aesthetic.
The entry door from garage to house you know with self closer. So, this is another detail
that was worked out for this kind of a project. So, there are oversized casement windows that
we were talking about in the previous slide also. There is vinyl sliding patio door with screen you
know or a double door those kinds of details are also here. Executive style front door grip set
these are like all very interesting details. So, when we talk about interior design projects
we must include what kind of window it is, what kind of material is being used, what kind of
finish do we see over here, is there any kind of paneling, are they sliding or not sliding,
is there any hardware detail that we see. So, all of these details have to be worked out and therefore
interior architecture drawings are also quite demanding. So, when we see interior design drawings
and representation techniques there we will probably discuss some of these. So, it is like you
know God is in the details. The drawings have to be like really elaborate with each little detail,
all inventories, all door window schedules, every kind of small to big detail has to be given along
with the specification, material detail, dimension everything. And so, like in the case of tiles we
will see whether it is a herringbone pattern or what is it. So, all those things we have to
put together when we are producing the interior architecture drawings.
Then there are also some exquisite floor finishes that we see in this project. So,
there are ceramic or porcelain tiles and there is oak flooring, we will see some of these when we
talk about the tiling. And there are also some non-tiled areas and they have very interesting
custom made and you know exquisite carpets. There are also some very interesting bathroom finishes
which are very very luxurious you know. There is a freestanding tub, there are ceramic wall tiles,
there are separate shower stalls which are used over here. There are also very interesting light
fixtures and you know frameless glass enclosures that we see in these bathrooms in this kind of
a project. There is also you know a dual shower head that we see in the room and then it is
repeated in several rooms. Also there are premium single lever faucets that we see in bathrooms.
There are soaker tubs that we see over here. So, these are all meant for you know luxury finishes
and sort of just being relaxed and having some interesting details. There are some
finishes that you see over here also in case of the vanity. So, there are oversized vanity
mirrors in all bathrooms and they are very very important and interesting finishes.
Also we see in the laundry you know some kind of interesting details whether it is the tub or the
faucet or even the heavy duty wiring and the vent for the dryer that we see even that has
very interesting finish. So, it requires a tremendous amount of detailing for a project like this.
Then there are gourmet kitchen finishes over here. We see very custom designed carp,
pantry and cabinets and we see some you know interesting stainless steel kitchen sink over
here and again some kind of very interesting hardware, plumbing equipment all of them have
some kind of a very very premium luxury finish. Like I was talking about plumbing,
dishwasher, sink, cabinets, storage units and the kind of finishes that have been adopted
for them even the countertops. They have been chosen with great care. Now completely
contrast to the luxury interiors we are now going to talk about the low cost interiors and there
are some examples from India specifically Rajasthan, Gujarat, Thir Pradesh maybe there is an example
from Uttarakhand also if I remember correctly. So, this is you know one house which is from
Rajasthan and specifically Jodhpur very very famous typology of residence and again
low cost in the sense that there are locally available materials. It is done by the community.
It is very very you know climate responsive and quite documented and decoded and understood in
terms of passive design features. But also the overall form and the aesthetic in terms of you
know surface finishes and wall finishes that we see over here that is also very interesting.
Then some kinds of you know paintings that we see in Rajasthan all sorts of houses these paintings
or wall finishes done by communities some of them are called as Marna paintings which are done by women
and this is from a house you know in a village near Jodhpur again in Rajasthan.
So, basically they are not just for aesthetic they are also you know
anti-termite they also provide some kind of an insulating layer they also look very beautiful
and they are very cool to touch at. So, these are very very interesting details from low cost
community based housing interiors from you know India. This is another example and that we see
over here. We see a lot of geometric designs sometimes non-geometric designs you know motifs
and patterns on these houses this one is from Jaisalmeer and it uses some beautiful colour pigments
and these get accentuated against the backdrop of you know of white.
And some more examples and it is not just wall finishes and surface finishes
low cost interiors can also be achieved in terms of other details specifically focusing on
materiality you know using something like ringal which is a species of bamboo which is found in
Uttarakhand or some kind of recycling of material or procuring some materials which are available
nearby and then trying to create some kind of interesting designs out of it. So, it could be
in terms of materiality it could be in terms of the scale it could be in terms of who are the
stakeholders is it done by the community themselves or is it done by someone who is formally trained
in interior architecture all of that all of those factors are also important, but typically these are
all low cost interiors which are very very functional which have elaborate interesting forms
and they are quite aesthetic. This is another one Barmeer again in Rajasthan and again a beautiful
you know use of colour surface finishes the kind of forms geometry definition at the entrance
and sight lines leading to the interior. So, again interesting spaces this is a restored
Haveli and this is near Jaipur this also has very very interesting details in terms of the
material that is used the kinds of furnishings textiles floor pattern etcetera. So, this is
again an interesting example. This is also a Haveli which is restored to its original state
and here also we see a very interesting colour palette the kind of finishes on the walls,
the vernacular furniture and the elements which are synonymous of critical regionalism
and a very very distinct style of interior architecture. This is another one where we see
this pink finished plaster over here and a very very beautiful hand beaten
brass bathroom sink and which adds you know amazing contrast and you know detail to this space and
the eye catches the attention because of this kind of a detail. Another project here where we see you
know details of timber on the ceiling, interesting utensils the arrangement of the objects in the
space the kind of detail over here on the furniture pieces and you know the kind of colour scheme that
we see over here and all the furniture has a very very distinct vocabulary. So, this is from Gujarat
this is a traditional pole house and this is also a very interesting piece of interior space.
This is another one which you know where there is a traditional mud floor over here
and there is also a contrasting you know magnificently painted ceiling and again a very
interesting furniture piece over here and this is also from the pole house in Ahmedabad and this
furniture is very distinct and we do not normally have these pieces of furniture readily available
in the market these days. So, it is very interesting to document and study these pieces of furniture.
Professor Jayat Huckar from SEPT is already doing this very amazing project
where he is documenting the vernacular furniture from across India and we at IIT Roorkee are also
trying to do this you know for the state of Uttarakhand and we are slowly building on that.
So, a furniture piece or the set of furniture has a profound role within an interior space and
it is very important to sort of document these kinds of you know furniture items or sort of
have a catalogue or understand the evolution and history or influences from different styles or
different people who came to India and brought these styles with them and vice versa. This is
the kitchen area again we see you know very interesting traditional brass cooking utensils
and they add a lot of interesting you know play in this entire space. So,
it is not just the structure, but also the surface finishes the decorative items,
the utilitarian items and the overall composition that is achieved by their placement that creates an
interior space and you know these static items could create a dynamism by the virtue of where
they are placed at what I levels and what are you know plays in the front and which are placed at
the back and so on. So, composition matters a lot. This is another project which is very interesting
and what is interesting over here is that the materials are actually reclaimed and then they
are sort of repurposed here. This is also an example from the state of Gujarat and I like this
project. Another one again from Gujarat where we see mud reliefs, we see mirror work, we see very
very interesting indigenous style of you know interior architecture which is very representative
of Ahmedabad and Gujarat. The Bhunga style of interior architecture, the Bhunga houses they
are quite known and extensively talked about. So, this is that example. Some more images of that.
This is another project. This is Dheradun Uttarakhand and here we see colonial style bed
and traditional blinds over here. So, this is also very interesting detailing. Then there is this
outdoor cafe. This is Triveni terrace cafe. It is one of my favorite projects. This is a New Delhi.
This is designed by Stein, a very famous architect and it is actually a part of Triveni Kala Sangam
where there are lots of cultural events that happen, the exhibitions that are being put up
and it is a very very interesting space, modern architecture style, use of interesting
Jali patterns, very interesting play of light and shadow and this cafeteria specifically is
very interesting. So, you know these exposed concrete finishes against you know the landscape
green that is very very interesting and from here there is a view to the OAT and outside
seating and this is the interior and from here we are looking towards outside. So,
there are both kinds of seatings inside and outside and there is also this interesting
you know use of bamboo and we see these exposed concrete beams and structural details and bamboo
and concrete sort of form this very interesting vocabulary for this entire cafeteria. There are
some international commercial projects where we can see interesting interior architecture details
like this one which is a museum and it is 1000 square feet and here the primary desire was to
you know be ecological and how to have more accessible spaces. So, it was very interesting
and the renovation was done for men's and women's facilities and there is a lot of attention given
to the children. So, baby changing tables, diaper disposal etc. Those important aspects were really
taken care of and they are very interesting plumbing details, very interesting fittings
and there is an attempt to you know have a very minimal use of water and to be very ecological
and to be very very responsible in the usage of resources. There is also this interesting
you know great arizo floor and it is a contemporary take on the 1933 wings original brown version
and that has been used here. So, functionality and aesthetics they go hand in hand in this project
and it is used by a lot of people including school groups. So, it is designed with a lot of care.
Then there is hotel okura this is a Tokyo based project and it has these interesting
exterior you know horizontal forms and there is this also you know the juxtaposition with the garden
and it is an interesting placement of modern material and the landscape outside.
I also find this very interesting detail you know the elevator doors which have the
surface finishes with the silk and textiles. There is a bamboo grove outside and there are
paper window screens and very beautiful space over here very elegantly designed and composed
and there is also you know the pine cladding there are structural columns which have these
kinds of cladding that we see over here. So, these material details make all the difference. We also
see these pendant fixtures you know they mimic the shape of beads which are popular from ancient
Japan and they were found in Japanese tomes and they are used here in a very metaphoric and
interesting manner. There is a patchwork wall that we see over here which again incorporates the silk
brocades and you know some interesting textiles dating as back as 13th century. So, this again is a
fusion of traditional and contemporary design and very sensibly using these elements and not
sort of diluting their importance or not sort of creating unpleasant appearance out of them,
but giving them a lot of respect and creating a very interesting design vocabulary out of them.
Again we were talking about the profound use and importance of hardware you know in interior
architecture projects. So, we see over here doors and you know they have like metal pulls
and they are also very interesting and eye-catching elements. There are also
leaded glass panels and they add on this entire orchid bar in this project. I love these hammered
copper sconches and they are very interesting texture over here and then also the you know
the difference in the color because of the way the lighting is designed and again there may be
also the difference in the gauge of copper or the sheet of copper that is chosen to create this
kind of design vocabulary. This is you know screen which is a cedar screen and it is designed to
give an appearance of a hemp leaf pattern and this also looks like quite aesthetic over here.
Then there is also a use of shells and these shells you know the shells lining a screen in
this orchid room restaurant also looks very very fantastic. These shells over here.
We also see a wall in the lobby where there is this world clock and it has been
trustingly put in place over here and I also like the use of colors that we see in this space
along with the lighting that has been designed and there are more images and more details over
here. There is a cloak room which is you know put next to a new stand and there are very interesting
details. There is a shop in the basement and more of these material aspects and you know
ceiling details and these furnishings over here that we see. Some more images from the project
very interesting and nicely designed project. Then there is a commercial project from India
and this one is in a good gown and this is a couture showroom and here again there is very
interesting use of material pallet. So there is a rough gaudier stone there is antique woodwork
that we see over here. It is a stone over here pieces of wood antique furniture and you know
there is wrought iron grill and there are wooden windows. There is this interesting installation
of spinning wheels and there is this yarn that comes out of these wheels and then it extends
and expands in space to create this sort of an interesting element of design. So those kinds
of installations are also interesting over here. Again elements like door handles, other hardware
elements also the signage and identity design everything put together plus the way the original
pattern and the finish of materials has been explored to the best advantage that is also
very interesting to see in this project. And there is a lot of tempt over here to highlight
make in India and there is this entire vocabulary where Indian designs or indigenous designs are
being highlighted. So it is an interesting project that way. Another one is Brick School of Architecture
Pune. This is also an interesting interior architecture project which does get inspiration
from the vernacular architecture of old city of Pune but it is also put together in a contemporary
manner. So again a very interesting fusion and its multi-purpose spaces are seen here which
are designed very elegantly. There is a series of port yards which is connecting the studios,
overlooking the corridors and it creates a beautiful imagery and a very interesting series
of sensory experiences and user experiences while one navigates from one space to another.
So these are only very few projects. There are actually many that can be discussed and I am sure
in other lectures during other modules we will also see many other examples and images and case
studies. I am just going to leave all of us with this thought might be very famous Charles Eames.
The details are not the details they make the design. So God is in the details and details
are very important to create remarkable designs that register us. We will be seeing the summary in
the next lecture for the last few lectures that we discussed and these are some of the references
that you may find useful and if you have to you know look further for these projects and more
details which I could not cover due to the restriction of time. Thank you very much. I will see you for
the next lecture.
